category_title: Students who strategically refuse special education services to avoid stigma
minimal_context: The student is taking an exam at their desk in the regular classroom while an instructional aide is present.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your exam. Please begin working on it at your desk.

STUDENT: I'ma just let it go and do it here.

TUTOR: You haven't started yet. Let me look at your paper.

STUDENT: I don't even bother anymore. You're just not gonna understand.

TUTOR: Well, just let me help you. (Reaches to take the test)

STUDENT: (Grabs the paperwork and pulls it towards himself) No, I don't need your help - I don't want your help. I'm not - nah - get out of here.

options.A: Progressively and methodically tune the student's awareness to each body part, intentionally relaxing each part from their toes to their head.
options.B: Provide a clear beginning and end for each section of the exam to structure the testing session.
options.C: Advocate for and collaborate with the student to provide the support they need in the general education classroom.
options.D: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation during the exam, such as a stress-relief ball.
